visual_action: A slideshow of still images. It begins with a photo of Donald Trump and Matt Gaetz speaking to each other outdoors. The video then transitions through a series of stock photos: an empty hospital room, a child eating a school lunch, a teacher in a classroom with students raising their hands, and a suburban house. Each image has text overlaid on it.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: He is shown in the opening photograph of the video, and the post implicitly critiques a war associated with him.

cast.name: Pentagon
cast.evidence: The on-screen text states, 'Pentagon officials are now estimating the Iran War has cost $100 billion'.

cast.name: Matt Gaetz
cast.evidence: He is visible in the first photograph standing next to Donald Trump.

on_screen_text.text: Pentagon officials are now estimating the Iran War has cost $100 billion
Here is what that could pay for
A year of healthcare for 10.8 million Americans
Two and a half years of free lunches for every public school student
A $31,250 raise for every public teacher
Affordable housing for over 12.5 million Americans

spoken_summary: There is no spoken dialogue in the video, only background music.
audio_music: A continuous, melancholic rock song ('Let Down' by Radiohead) plays throughout the video, creating a somber and serious mood that underscores the theme of opportunity cost.
editing_pacing: The video is a slow-paced slideshow, transitioning between five static images.
central_claim: The $100 billion cost of the Iran War is a misallocation of funds that could have instead paid for vital domestic programs like healthcare, school lunches, teacher raises, and housing for millions of Americans.
intended_effect: To persuade the viewer that the war is a tragic waste of resources and to generate opposition to the political figures associated with it by highlighting the domestic benefits that were forgone.
